title: Asset health and predictive maintenance
summary: A raw water pump develops bearing degradation. Edge IQ detects the trend, classifies it against ISO 10816-3, estimates remaining useful life and drafts a work order that a planner must approve.

iqLayers.fabricIq: Vibration history and the asset record, resolved through the water ontology.
iqLayers.foundryIq: ISO 10816-3 severity bands and the pump overhaul SOP.
iqLayers.workIq: Prior Teams threads and the maintenance plan for this asset.

seededFault.behaviour: Exponential rise beginning 12 days ago, reaching 7.9 mm/s today.
seededFault.why: 7.9 mm/s puts a 75 kW machine in ISO 10816-3 zone D - unacceptable, damage is occurring. The >75 kW band (C/D limit 11.0) would call the same value zone C, which is why the agent must read rated power from the asset registry rather than assume a threshold.

script.ask: Vibration on WTP-01-PUMP-003 has been climbing. What is the ISO 10816-3 zone, and what should we do?
script.expect: Routes to asset-health. Reads rated power (75 kW) from the asset registry, places 7.9 mm/s in zone D, and cites the ISO 10816-3 knowledge article.
script.watchFor: The route panel should name asset-health, and the evidence list should include the ISO standard - not just telemetry. An answer with no standard cited is pattern-matching, not engineering.

script.ask: How long have we got before it fails?
script.expect: Extrapolates the trend and gives a window with its basis stated, rather than a single confident date.
script.watchFor: Conversation memory - the device is not restated, so the turn only works if history carried forward.

script.ask: What does our SOP say about a zone D pump, and has anyone already raised this?
script.expect: Foundry IQ returns the overhaul SOP; Work IQ surfaces related M365 activity (placeholder text until Graph is connected).
script.watchFor: The Work IQ layer pill reads 'placeholder' in demo mode. That is the honest answer, not a failure.

script.ask: Raise a work order for a bearing replacement at the next planned outage.
script.expect: maintenance-planner drafts the work order but does NOT commit it. The approval panel appears.
script.watchFor: pendingApprovals is populated and committed is false. Writes need approved=true AND EDGEIQ_ALLOW_WRITES=true - two independent keys, so neither a model nor a UI click can act alone.

talkingPoints: The severity band is read from the asset record, not hardcoded. Change the pump's rated power and the same reading changes zone.
Every recommendation carries its evidence. Operators can check the standard rather than trusting the model.
The write is gated. Edge IQ prepares work, a human commits it.
